transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: ~36 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ross (Redwood SE), Sophie Liu (Aurelia - Head of ML), Carlos Mendes (Aurelia - Infra), Leah Bryant (Aurelia - PM)

Summary:
Quick onboarding/check-in focused on access and environment readiness for the POC bench. Agreed next week for a 2-hour benchmark run, resolved SSO/KMS questions, and outlined tasks for staging access. Some small clarifications around dedicated vs hosted cost tradeoffs and network egress.

Topics:
- Staging access & VPN creds
- SSO/SAML and KMS integration questions
- Benchmark schedule and test prompts
- Early tuning: quantization, batching, KV-cache hints
- Security docs (SOC2, audit logs)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we wanted to do a quick 30 minute check-in, but looks like people had time so we'll do a bit longer, uh quick roll call?
[00:08] Sophie: Sophie here, hi, yep thanks Maya.
[00:11] Carlos: Carlos on infra, morning.
[00:13] Leah: Leah, PM.
[00:15] Ethan: Ethan from Redwood, hi all.
[00:17] Maya: great, thanks. quick agenda: access status, any blockers for staging run, security docs, then benchmark windows and roles.
[00:25] Sophie: on access, we tried the staging creds from last week but our SSO redirect kept failing, error said - redirect_uri mismatch. we think it's my auth config but wanted to confirm what's expected on Redwood's side.
[00:35] Maya: ok that rings a bell; we updated the SSO docs yesterday, there was a mismatch in the callback url we gave you. i can re-send the updated SSO setup guide, it includes the exact redirect and the metadata xml for SAML.
[00:45] Carlos: that would help. also, for the Private deployment path we might need to confirm KMS access — our security team requires customer-managed keys in KMS/HSM. what's the integration story there?
[00:56] Ethan: good question. for Private we support external KMS via standard kms api, we have docs for a BYOK flow. for Dedicated we have a dedicated KMS config option too, but if you're on hosted we can do envelope encryption and keep CMKs in your cloud project. i'll put the doc link in the notes, but essentially you can mount your key via our customer key provider.
[01:20] Sophie: ok, so for the POC we probably want to try staging with hosted but with a customer-managed key to satisfy security — is that feasible?
[01:28] Ethan: yeah that's feasible; the one caveat is if you want hardware-backed HSM in your own VPC it takes a little setup time. for the pilot we can emulate it with cloud KMS CMK and later swap to HSM if you proceed.
[01:40] Leah: timeline wise we want benchmarks this coming week, ideally Monday or Tuesday — what's your availability?
[01:47] Maya: we suggested week of 8/10 in the deck, Ethan do you have capacity for a 2-hour run early in the week?
[01:53] Ethan: yes i can run it Tues morning PST, we'll need staging creds and the canonical prompt set from Leah so we can reproduce latency and quality.
[02:05] Sophie: quick note on network: our staging is behind a restricted egress policy; we might need a temporary VPN or whitelist Redwood IPs. carlos can confirm.
[02:12] Carlos: correct. i've started a ticket to open egress to Redwood staging and to provide a VPN account, should have creds by thursday night, maybe earlier.
[02:21] Maya: perfect — for the benchmark we'll ask you to allow outbound to our staging address and to open the needed ports; ethan will send a short port list.
[02:30] Ethan: ports 443 outbound, plus ssh 22 if you want a debug bastion, but not strictly required; i'll send exact ip ranges.
[02:38] Leah: on success metrics, we're looking for p95 latency under 700ms for our 512-token avg case and cost per 1k tokens to be under our target — i'll add exact numbers in the shared sheet.
[02:49] Maya: sounds good, that helps define the tuning knobs — batching and quantization profile recommendations will vary depending on whether you use Dedicated or Hosted.
[02:58] Sophie: can you remind us of the differences — we want to keep data in our environment but also want the performance benefits of Dedicated.
[03:05] Ethan: yes, Hosted is fastest to start, no infra work, but you give up some isolation. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and lower jitter/latency; Private (VPC) gives full network isolation and BYOK. in terms of tuning, Dedicated allows more aggressive batching and longer KV cache sessions because we can keep warm shards for your tenant.
[03:26] Sophie: that's helpful. for the POC, we were thinking Hosted + CMK to get up quickly and then move to Dedicated if numbers look good.
[03:33] Maya: that is a common path. also note we can do a mixed routing policy so critical traffic hits Dedicated and other traffic routes to Hosted to save cost — but that is more of an ops config later.
[03:46] Carlos: i'm still concerned about audit logs — do you keep token-level logs? our compliance requires redaction and retention controls.
[03:53] Ethan: yes we have per-route trace hooks and configurable retention. by default we don't persist full raw inputs for longer than X days (will attach policy), and we can enable redaction and token-level cost breakdowns for your team. i'll include the audit logs spec in the security pack.
[04:10] Sophie: great, SOC 2 and that audit doc are the main asks from our infosec.
[04:15] Maya: i'll send SOC2 report and the security deck after this call.
[04:18] Leah: perfect. small question on model versions — we saw some references to "redwood-ggml" in the early notes, is that accurate?
[04:25] Ethan: heh the naming in the older docs got messy — we have model variants and quantized builds, sometimes internal names leak through, we'll give you the production catalog view. for the bench we'll point to the model id and exact artifact.
[04:39] Sophie: ok, and for the bench run can you also test a quantized 4-bit variant? we want to see the latency/cost tradeoff.
[04:46] Ethan: yes we can run both full fp16 and a 4-bit quantized variant. expectation is quantized will drop memory/throughput needs and reduce cost but may slightly change outputs; we'll include a quick eval on your prompt set.
[04:59] Maya: on the staging creds — carlos will provide VPN creds — will those be long lived or short lived?
[05:05] Carlos: short lived, i'll give a 72-hour window tied to the benchmark run.
[05:09] Leah: ok that works.
[05:11] Sophie: anything else on tuning? we had asked about KV cache — how persistent is it across requests?
[05:18] Ethan: we support per-session KV caching; on Dedicated we can keep cache warm between requests for same tenant for as long as the session token is alive, hosted has more eviction due to multi-tenant packing. for your workload if you have a lot of prefix reuse it's beneficial to be on Dedicated.
[05:36] Sophie: noted.
[05:38] Maya: quick run through of next steps: i'll email SOC2 + security deck + updated SSO guide; ethan will send ip ranges and port list and then we'll lock a benchmark slot for Tuesday 8/11 AM; carlos to provide VPN creds by 8/6 and leah will drop prompt set and metrics by 8/9.
[05:58] Carlos: that's the plan. one more quick question — about costs, the pricing sheet had a note about burst capacity, can you remind us how burst billing works?
[06:07] Maya: sure, for Dedicated you commit to reserved capacity; burst is an extra cost when you exceed the pool, billed at a higher rate. for Hosted you pay per token and can scale but costs are variable; we'll send an updated pricing worksheet with examples tied to your expected throughput.
[06:23] Leah: will that worksheet include examples of batching and tokenization impact?
[06:27] Ethan: yes we'll include a small sensitivity table that shows p95 latency vs batch size and cost per 1k tokens.
[06:33] Sophie: excellent.
[06:35] Maya: ok if there are no other blockers we'll wrap. thanks everyone — expect the security pack and SSO guide in inbox in a few hours.
[06:43] Sophie: thanks, looking forward.
[06:44] Carlos: thanks all.
[06:45] Leah: thanks.

End of transcript.
